title: Minimum Number of Refills (Parenthesization DP)
statement:
Given a chain of matrices to multiply, where matrix `i` has dimensions `p[i-1] x p[i]`, find the minimum number of scalar multiplications needed to compute the product.
This is the classic Matrix Chain Multiplication problem solved via Interval DP.
inputFormat:
Line 1: an integer N (number of matrices = N-1 where N = length of dimension array).
Line 2: N space-separated integers representing the dimension array `p`.
outputFormat: A single integer: the minimum multiplication cost.

starterCode.python:
n = int(input())
p = list(map(int, input().split()))
# dp[i][j] = min cost to multiply matrices i..j
